title.text: Pink Beach, Great Santa Cruz Island (Zamboanga)

title_en.text: Pink Beach, Great Santa Cruz Island (Zamboanga)

tagline.text: Pale pink sand tinted by crushed red coral, on a small protected island off Zamboanga

location.label: Location
location.text: Great Santa Cruz Island in the Basilan Strait, south of Zamboanga City (about 15 minutes by boat from the Paseo del Mar jetty)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱150–700 (island day trip, based on shared boat, entrance fee, cottage and mangrove tour; excluding city transport)

children.text: This is the pink-sand beach on Great Santa Cruz Island, reached by boat from Paseo del Mar in Zamboanga. Crushed red coral gives the pale sand its color. Visitor numbers are limited, so confirm your boat and return time before going.

Great Santa Cruz Island lies in the Basilan Strait south of Zamboanga City. The beach where fragments of organ-pipe coral mix with white sand is known as Pink Beach. The color changes with sunlight and tide. See the
Great Santa Cruz Island guide
for the island’s setting and other stops.

Little Santa Cruz Island next door and Great Santa Cruz Island were declared a Protected Landscape and Seascape on April 23, 2000, by Proclamation No. 271, and the protected area covers 1,877 hectares. That is why taking coral from the beach is prohibited. In the past, illegal coral mining damaged much of the reef, and the city has announced plans to restore the island as an ecotourism site using low buildings made of local materials.
Book in advance through the Protected Area Management Office (PAMO) at Paseo del Mar. The
city’s official visitor guide
lists the booking number +63 905 601 6316. Show your booking reference and complete the passenger manifest. Walk-ins join a standby list.

There is no accommodation on the island, so it can only be a day trip, and there is almost nowhere to buy food. The usual plan is to rest in a cottage with a packed lunch and drinks, walk on the sand and take photos, and optionally take a mangrove tour. The color of the sand looks different depending on weather, light and photo editing, so expect a soft pale pink rather than a vivid pink. According to Wikipedia, travelers from Germany, Italy, Japan and elsewhere began visiting the island in the 1970s and early 1980s, and domestic tourism has grown considerably in recent years. The city has projected that restoring the island's ecosystem and growing ecotourism will take 3 to 5 years. In other words, the rules and facilities are still changing, so the most accurate approach is to check with the tourism office just before you go.

Sand mixed with pieces of red coral forms a pale pink band along the water's edge. Many reviews say the color shows best when you shoot low from the waterline. In strong midday sun the sand can look white, so aim for the morning.

The mangrove lagoon tour is booked separately from beach admission. Ask the Protected Area Management Office for departure times, boat and guide charges, and whether each charge is per person or per boat.

On one side of the island there is a small sandbar, and the time you can walk on it depends on the tide. Check the tide times before you go. The sandbar sometimes appears only at low tide, so the window to visit is limited.
As of March 2024, a small cottage is ₱100, a large cottage ₱200 and the pavilion ₱500. There is little shade, so renting a cottage gives you a good place to rest and leave your things.

Badjao people live on the island. Because it is their home, ask permission before taking photos and move quietly through residential areas. The Badjao are commonly known as a people who have lived with the sea.

The Santa Cruz Islands are a protected landscape and seascape. You will see shells and coral fragments along the shore, but they cannot be taken away; following the rules is how this place is preserved for the long term. Both islands were designated together, covering 1,877 hectares.

Boats leave from the Paseo del Mar jetty in the city, and the ride takes about 15–20 minutes. The tourism office is at the same jetty, so you can book and complete formalities in one place. It is easy to combine with Fort Pilar in the city in a single day.

items.subtitle: In the morning, out before lunch

children.text: Have breakfast at your hotel and bring only a small bag and a packed lunch. Do not bring single-use plastics.
Show your booking reference and fill in the passenger manifest at PAMO. When called, attend the protected-area briefing and board the assigned boat.
Listen to the rules briefing and board the boat. The ride to the island takes about 15–20 minutes.
Take photos on the beach, claim a cottage, then explore the sandbar and the mangroves.
Eat your packed lunch and rest.
Board your return boat at the meeting time in the booking instructions.
Back in the city, see Fort Pilar and visit a seafood restaurant.
If the weather turns bad, boats may not run, so leave some slack in your schedule.

Cebu Pacific and PAL Express operate nonstop flights from Manila (MNL) to Zamboanga International Airport (ZAM).
Flight time is about
1 hour 40 minutes–1 hour 55 minutes
depending on the route-information site. Schedules change, so check when booking.
The distance between Manila and Zamboanga is about 850 km.
One guide says 2GO passenger ferries take about two days from Manila to the Zamboanga port. Check the latest information on whether the service is running.
From the airport, take a tricycle or taxi into the city. Confirm fares locally.
Take a tricycle from the city to Paseo del Mar as well.

items.title: From the jetty to the island

children.text: Board a motorized banca at the Paseo del Mar jetty. The ride takes about
15–20 minutes
Confirm the return boat fare and passenger capacity when booking. Pay the boat operator directly.
The boat fare is based on a 2022 article, so confirm it locally.

The November–May dry season of the Philippines is the most reliable. The sea is calm and the skies are clear, which suits photos of the pink tint. On cloudy days the sand color can look faint, so a clear morning is best for photos.

In the rainy season, waves and rain have kept boats from running and left visitors stranded. In August 2022, 42 visitors were reportedly rescued after heavy rain and waves. Check the weather forecast and follow staff instructions.
Confirm your outbound and return sailings and the time you must leave the island when booking. Bring your booking reference to the protected-area office at Paseo del Mar to check in.

There is no lodging on the island, so stay in Zamboanga City and visit as a day trip. The area near Paseo del Mar is the most convenient for getting around. The city has a wide range of hotels and guesthouses. Staying in the city the night before makes it much easier to reach the jetty in time for the first boat.

Almost no food is sold on the island, so bring a packed lunch and water in reusable containers rather than single-use ones. One guide says there is nowhere on the island to buy food and drinks. Back in the city, you can try local food, including seafood, at many restaurants in Zamboanga.

When planning your day, the most practical approach is to prepare a packed lunch, water and snacks in advance at your hotel or from city shops. With no restaurants on the island apart from the cottages, you must also take all food waste back with you. Carry cash in small bills so it is easy to pay the entrance fee and cottage rental.
Before your visit, confirm bookings and whether visits are possible at the Zamboanga City tourism office or the protected area management office.
Single-use plastics are confiscated, so use reusable containers.
Confirm your outbound and return sailings and the time you must leave the island when booking. Bring your booking reference to the protected-area office at Paseo del Mar to check in.
Do not take away sand, shells or coral.
There is little shade, so bring a hat, sunscreen and water.
Checking the tide makes it easier to walk on the sandbar.
Prepare cash (small bills). Cards may not be accepted on the island.
Ask permission before photographing residents.
Going on the first boat helps you avoid the midday sun and the crowds.
You cannot stay on the island long, so plan your schedule in advance.
Foreign governments sometimes issue travel advisories for southwestern Mindanao, so check the latest advisories and your insurance conditions before departure.
Visitor numbers and weekly closures can change. There is information that in 2022 the island was closed on Mondays and Fridays for cleaning, so confirm.
If the waves are high, boats do not run. Follow the staff's instructions to return.
Prices differ between sources, so check the latest rate table on site.
Breaking the protected-area rules (single-use plastics, no collecting) can result in penalties.
Some articles say camping is free or cheap, but protected-area rules may have changed, so be sure to check whether it is allowed.
Residents' homes and boats are private property, so do not enter or touch them without permission.
A 17th-century Spanish fort and Marian shrine easily reached from the city. Adding it to your city plan makes the day flow naturally.
A neighboring island in the same protected area. Check with the tourism office whether it can be visited.
The jetty for the island and a waterfront park, good for an evening stroll.
